questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme:
1. It was introduced in 1998-99 on the basis of the recommendations of the R.V. Gupta Committee.
2. Its facility was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries farmers in 2018-19.
3. It can be issued only by commercial banks and not by cooperative banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: KCC was designed to give farmers timely, single-window short-term credit, and it was later widened to cover animal husbandry and fisheries working capital. Statement 3 is wrong because commercial banks, RRBs and cooperative banks all issue KCCs.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Agriculture chapter); NABARD

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Agriculture Market (eNAM):
1. It is a pan-India electronic trading portal that was launched in 2016.
2. The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) is the lead agency for its implementation.
3. It abolishes the existing APMC mandis and replaces them with online-only private markets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: eNAM networks existing regulated mandis into a common online platform so that buyers anywhere can bid, and SFAC under the Agriculture Ministry runs it. It does not abolish APMC mandis, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: e-NAM = mandis on a network, not mandis removed

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PM-KISAN:
1. It provides Rs 6,000 a year to eligible farmer families in three equal instalments.
2. It is a Central Sector scheme with 100 percent funding by the Union Government.
3. The money is transferred directly to the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
4. State governments bear 40 percent of the cost of the scheme.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-KISAN is an income-support scheme paid by Direct Benefit Transfer in instalments of Rs 2,000. It is fully funded by the Centre, so the claim of a 40 percent state share is wrong.
questions.s: PIB, PM-KISAN scheme guidelines; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: The National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan Commission) recommended that the Minimum Support Price be fixed at least 50 percent above a particular cost of production. In the Union Budget 2018-19 the Government announced MSP at 1.5 times a cost. Which one of the following correctly identifies the two costs?
o: Commission: A2 + FL cost; Budget: C2 cost
Commission: A2 cost; Budget: A2 + FL cost
Commission: C2 (comprehensive) cost; Budget: C2 cost
Commission: C2 (comprehensive) cost; Budget: A2 + FL cost
questions.e: The Swaminathan formula is C2 + 50 percent, where C2 includes imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital. The 2018-19 Budget formula used the lower A2 + FL cost (paid-out cost plus imputed family labour), which is why farmer groups say it falls short of the commission's recommendation.
questions.h: C2 is the Complete cost; A2+FL is the Actual-paid cost

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Organisation)
A. APEDA
B. NDDB
C. SFAC
D. NABARD
List-II (Administrative Ministry)
1. Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
2. Ministry of Commerce and Industry
3. Ministry of Finance
4. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
questions.e: APEDA promotes agri-exports and sits in Commerce; NDDB, the Operation Flood body, is under the dairying ministry; SFAC supports FPOs under the Agriculture Ministry; NABARD is under Finance (Department of Financial Services).

questions.q:
Statement-I: Micro irrigation methods such as drip and sprinkler systems are promoted under the 'Per Drop More Crop' component of PMKSY.
Statement-II: Micro irrigation applies water near the root zone, which reduces evaporation and conveyance losses compared with flood irrigation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Per Drop More Crop aims at higher water-use efficiency, and drip and sprinkler systems achieve it by delivering water to the root zone with little loss to evaporation and seepage. That physical advantage is the reason the government subsidises them.

questions.q: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of which one of the following?
questions.e: The Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development (CRAFICARD) under B. Sivaraman proposed a single apex body, and NABARD took over the refinance functions of RBI's agricultural credit department and the ARDC.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding priority sector lending (PSL) norms for domestic commercial banks as per RBI directions:
1. The overall priority sector target is 40 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit.
2. The sub-target for agriculture is 18 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit.
3. The sub-target for small and marginal farmers is 15 percent.
4. Regional Rural Banks have an overall priority sector target of 60 percent.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 40 percent overall and 18 percent agriculture targets are right. The small and marginal farmer sub-target is 10 percent, and RRBs must lend 75 percent to the priority sector, so statements 3 and 4 are wrong.
questions.s: RBI Master Direction on Priority Sector Lending; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
With reference to the Farmer Producer Organisations (FPO) scheme for formation and promotion of 10,000 FPOs, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2020.
2. SFAC, NABARD and NCDC are among its implementing agencies.
3. FPOs can be registered only as cooperative societies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme builds scale for small farmers by pooling input purchase and produce sale. FPOs can be registered as producer companies under the Companies Act or as cooperative societies, so 'only' makes statement 3 wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) is NOT correct?
o: It recommends Minimum Support Prices for mandated crops.
It recommends the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane.
It was known as the Agricultural Prices Commission before 1985.
It is a statutory body established under an Act of Parliament.
questions.e: CACP is an attached office of the Agriculture Ministry, not a statutory body, so its recommendations are advisory and the final MSP is decided by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs. It was created in 1965 as the Agricultural Prices Commission and renamed in 1985.

questions.q:
Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. Amber box subsidies are trade-distorting and are subject to reduction commitments.
2. Green box subsidies, such as decoupled income support, are exempt from reduction commitments.
3. The de minimis limit for developing countries is 5 percent of the value of production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Amber box measures like price support distort trade and must be reduced, while green box measures have minimal trade effect. The de minimis limit is 10 percent for developing countries and 5 percent for developed countries, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: Traffic light: Amber = caution, Green = go

questions.q:
Statement-I: Regulation of agricultural produce markets in India differs from state to state.
Statement-II: 'Markets and fairs' is an entry in the State List of the Seventh Schedule, and most states regulate mandis through their own APMC Acts.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because markets are a State List subject, each state wrote its own APMC law, which is why licensing, fees and exemptions vary. This fragmentation is what eNAM and the Model APMC Act 2003 and 2017 models tried to ease.

questions.q: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income, which submitted its report in 2018 on the strategy to double farmers' income by 2022-23, was headed by:
questions.e: The Government constituted the committee in 2016 under Ashok Dalwai after announcing the doubling target. M.S. Swaminathan headed the earlier National Commission on Farmers.

questions.q:
Which of the following are components of PM-KUSUM?
1. Setting up small decentralised grid-connected solar power plants on farmers' barren or fallow land
2. Installation of standalone solar agricultural pumps
3. Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
4. Setting up of wind farms on irrigation canals
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: PM-KUSUM, run by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, has three components: A (plants on farm land), B (standalone pumps) and C (solarising grid pumps). It helps farmers cut diesel and subsidised electricity use and earn from surplus power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF):
1. It provides medium to long-term debt financing for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
2. Loans under it carry an interest subvention of 3 percent per annum up to Rs 2 crore.
3. FPOs and agri-entrepreneurs are not eligible beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rs 1 lakh crore fund launched in 2020 targets cold chains, warehouses and primary processing to cut post-harvest losses. FPOs, farmers, PACS and agri-entrepreneurs are eligible, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Operation Greens:
1. It was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 to stabilise supply and prices of tomato, onion and potato.
2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Operation Greens mirrors Operation Flood for horticulture, with a focus on the TOP crops, whose prices swing sharply with seasonal gluts. The scheme sits with the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, which of the following approaches is adopted for cluster development?
questions.e: PMFME, launched in 2020 under Atmanirbhar Bharat, gives credit-linked capital subsidy to micro units and supports clusters built around a product that a district is known for, enabling common infrastructure and branding.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):
1. Farmers pay a maximum premium of 2 percent for kharif food crops and oilseeds.
2. The farmer premium for rabi food crops and oilseeds is 1.5 percent.
3. The premium for annual commercial and horticultural crops is capped at 5 percent.
4. Enrolment has been compulsory for all farmers since its inception.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Farmer premiums are fixed low at 2, 1.5 and 5 percent, with the balance shared by the Centre and states. Enrolment was made voluntary for all farmers in 2020, so it was never compulsory throughout and statement 4 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):
1. They were set up in 1975 on the recommendation of the Narasimham Working Group.
2. Their share capital is held by the Centre, the concerned State and a sponsor bank in the ratio 50:15:35.
3. NABARD acts as the sponsor bank of every RRB.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RRBs were created to combine local feel of cooperatives with commercial bank resources for weaker sections. Their sponsor banks are commercial banks, and NABARD only holds regulatory and refinance roles, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: In the short-term cooperative credit structure in India, which one of the following gives the correct order from the village level to the apex level?
o: PACS - District Central Cooperative Bank - State Cooperative Bank
District Central Cooperative Bank - PACS - State Cooperative Bank
PACS - State Cooperative Bank - District Central Cooperative Bank
State Cooperative Bank - District Central Cooperative Bank - PACS
questions.e: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies lend to farmers directly, district central cooperative banks federate the PACS, and the State Cooperative Bank sits at the top and links the system to NABARD and RBI. The long-term structure is separate, run through agriculture and rural development banks.

questions.q: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), maintained by NABARD, is financed mainly by contributions from:
o: Commercial banks that fall short of their priority sector or agricultural lending targets
State governments' share of Union taxes
Premium paid by farmers under crop insurance
questions.e: RIDF was set up in 1995-96 as a penalty-turned-resource arrangement: banks that miss their agriculture lending targets must deposit the shortfall with NABARD, which lends it to states for rural infrastructure such as irrigation and roads.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sugarcane pricing in India:
1. The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on the recommendation of the CACP.
2. FRP replaced the Statutory Minimum Price in 2009-10.
3. State governments are not permitted to announce a State Advised Price above the FRP.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FRP is the floor price payable by mills, set by the Centre under the Sugarcane (Control) Order. Some states such as Uttar Pradesh announce a higher State Advised Price, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT among the three Acts repealed by the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021?
o: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020
The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020
questions.e: The 2021 repeal removed the three laws of 2020 on trade areas outside APMC mandis, contract farming and stock limits. The 2007 Act that created the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority is a separate, still operating law.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Operation Flood:
1. It was launched in 1970 and implemented by the National Dairy Development Board.
2. It was based on the Anand pattern of a three-tier cooperative structure of village societies, district unions and a state federation.
3. The Anand pattern is a two-tier structure of village societies and a national federation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Operation Flood built a national milk grid by linking village producers to urban consumers, using the Amul model led by Verghese Kurien. The Anand model has three tiers, so the two-tier claim is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the fisheries sector in India:
1. India is the largest fish-producing country in the world.
2. Fisheries is a subject in the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
3. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was launched in 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fisheries is entry 21 of the State List, and PMMSY (2020) funds infrastructure, cold chains and productivity. India is the second largest fish producer after China, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a scheduled product for which the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) is responsible?
questions.e: APEDA promotes export of fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy, honey and basmati rice among others. Tea has its own commodity board, the Tea Board, while MPEDA handles marine products.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Commodity Board : Headquarters
1. Rubber Board : Kottayam
2. Coffee Board : Chikmagalur
3. Tea Board : Kolkata
4. Tobacco Board : Hyderabad
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Rubber Board is at Kottayam and the Tea Board at Kolkata. The Coffee Board is headquartered at Bengaluru and the Tobacco Board at Guntur, so those two pairs are wrong.

questions.q: Under the traditional classification of irrigation projects in India, a project is called 'major' when its culturable command area (CCA) exceeds:
questions.e: Major projects have CCA above 10,000 ha, medium ones lie between 2,000 and 10,000 ha, and minor ones are below 2,000 ha. Minor irrigation includes wells and tube wells, which supply the largest share of irrigation.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest source of irrigation in terms of net irrigated area in India?
questions.e: Groundwater structures serve the largest share of net irrigated area because they are farmer-controlled, reliable and spread across the Indo-Gangetic plain. Canals are second, which is why over-extraction and falling water tables are a major concern.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)?
questions.e: PMKSY brings together AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop and watershed development under one umbrella for 'end-to-end' irrigation. RKVY is a separate state-level agricultural development scheme begun in 2007.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about organic farming initiatives in India:
1. Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state in 2012.
2. The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana promotes cluster-based organic farming and Participatory Guarantee System certification.
3. The Mission Organic Value Chain Development scheme is meant for the North Eastern Region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PKVY and the North-East value chain mission support clusters with certification and market links. Sikkim was declared fully organic in 2016 after a phased state policy, so the year 2012 is wrong.

questions.q: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA), which regulates negotiable warehouse receipts, functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
questions.e: WDRA was set up under the 2007 Act, and it works under the Department of Food and Public Distribution. Negotiable receipts let farmers pledge stored produce for bank finance and avoid distress sales after harvest.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the PM-AASHA scheme:
1. It was approved in 2018 to ensure remunerative prices to farmers.
2. It includes the Price Support Scheme and the Price Deficiency Payment Scheme.
3. Its Price Support Scheme covers paddy and wheat procurement by the Food Corporation of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-AASHA widens price support beyond cereals to pulses, oilseeds and copra, with options like deficiency payment when market price falls below MSP. Paddy and wheat procurement is a separate MSP operation, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about fertiliser policy in India:
1. Phosphatic and potassic fertilisers have been subsidised under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme since 2010.
2. The maximum retail price of urea is fixed by the Government.
3. Neem coating of urea is meant to increase its nitrogen content.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under NBS the subsidy is set per kg of nutrient, whereas urea remains under price control with a fixed MRP. Neem coating slows nitrogen release and curbs diversion to industry; it does not raise nitrogen content, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Only a small share of India's farmers actually sell their produce to government agencies at the Minimum Support Price.
Statement-II: Open-ended public procurement at MSP has operated mainly for paddy and wheat, and largely in a few states.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Since effective procurement is concentrated in two cereals and a handful of states, most farmers of other crops and regions do not receive the MSP in practice. The Shanta Kumar High Level Committee on FCI (2015) estimated that only about 6 percent of farmers benefit from MSP procurement.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh; Shanta Kumar Committee Report on FCI, 2015

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Ministry of Cooperation was created by the Union Government in July 2021.
Statement-II: The 97th Constitutional Amendment made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right and added Article 43B in the Directive Principles.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
questions.e: Both statements are true, but the 2011 amendment did not create the 2021 ministry; the ministry was set up to give cooperatives a separate administrative and policy focus. Cooperative societies remain a State subject, so the amendment and the ministry are independent steps.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India is the largest producer of milk in the world.
Statement-II: India is also the largest exporter of milk products in the world.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Operation Flood and the cooperative network made India the top milk producer, but most of the output is consumed domestically. India's dairy exports are small compared with those of countries such as New Zealand, so Statement-II is wrong.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (ICAR Institute)
A. Central Potato Research Institute
B. Central Rice Research Institute
C. Sugarcane Breeding Institute
D. Indian Institute of Spices Research
List-II (Location)
1. Coimbatore
2. Kozhikode
3. Shimla
4. Cuttack
questions.e: Potato research is based in the cool hills of Shimla, rice research at Cuttack in the rice belt of Odisha, sugarcane breeding at Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu and spices research at Kozhikode in Kerala.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Revolution)
A. Yellow Revolution
B. Silver Revolution
C. Blue Revolution
D. Golden Revolution
List-II (Focus)
1. Fisheries
2. Oilseeds
3. Horticulture and honey
4. Eggs and poultry
questions.e: Yellow refers to mustard and other oilseeds, silver to eggs, blue to fish and golden to fruits, vegetables and honey.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
A. Shanta Kumar Committee
B. Vaidyanathan Committee
C. Swaminathan Commission
D. R.V. Gupta Committee
List-II (Subject)
1. Kisan Credit Card design
2. Restructuring of the Food Corporation of India
3. Revival of rural cooperative credit institutions
4. MSP at 50 percent above comprehensive cost of production
questions.e: Shanta Kumar's panel examined FCI procurement and stocking, Vaidyanathan's 2004 panel proposed a revival package for cooperative credit, Swaminathan's commission proposed the C2 plus 50 percent formula, and Gupta's group shaped the KCC.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana:
1. Mega Food Parks under it follow a hub-and-spoke model with a central processing centre and primary processing centres.
2. The scheme supports integrated cold chain infrastructure from farm gate to consumer.
3. It is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme builds processing and cold-chain capacity to cut post-harvest losses and raise farmers' realisation. It is run by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
With reference to India's agricultural trade, consider the following statements:
1. The Agriculture Export Policy 2018 aimed to double agricultural exports to about 60 billion US dollars by 2022.
2. India is the largest exporter of rice in the world.
3. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority regulates exports of marine products.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The export policy set a doubling target to push value-added exports, and India overtook Thailand as the top rice exporter. Marine products are handled by MPEDA, not APEDA, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: The decision of the WTO membership to eliminate agricultural export subsidies was taken at which Ministerial Conference?
questions.e: The Nairobi Ministerial Decision on Export Competition committed developed countries to remove export subsidies immediately and developing countries later. The Bali conference is remembered for the Trade Facilitation Agreement and the interim peace clause on public stockholding.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NABARD:
1. It provides refinance to banks and cooperative institutions for agriculture and rural development.
2. It supervises Regional Rural Banks and cooperative banks.
3. Its share capital is wholly held by the Reserve Bank of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NABARD works as an apex refinance and supervisory body rather than lending directly to farmers. Since 2010 its capital has been held by the Government of India after RBI sold its stake, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs of crops are both kharif crops?
1. Soybean
2. Mustard
3. Cotton
4. Barley
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon and harvested in autumn, and soybean and cotton fit this pattern. Mustard and barley are sown in winter and harvested in spring, which makes them rabi crops.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII, India: People and Economy; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Green Revolution widened regional disparities in agricultural development in India.
Statement-II: The new high-yielding variety technology was largely confined to wheat and rice grown in assured irrigation areas such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: HYV seeds needed assured water and fertiliser, so they spread first where irrigation existed, leaving rainfed regions and crops such as pulses and coarse cereals behind. This uneven spread is why the benefits were concentrated regionally.

questions.q: Which one of the following crops is NOT covered by the Minimum Support Price announced by the Central Government?
questions.e: MSP is announced for selected cereals, pulses, oilseeds and commercial crops such as cotton, jute and copra. Potato and other perishable vegetables and fruits have no MSP, which is why Operation Greens addresses their price swings differently.

questions.q:
Consider the following reforms that states are required to adopt in their APMC laws to join eNAM:
1. Provision for electronic auction as a mode of price discovery
2. A single trading licence valid across the state
3. Single-point levy of market fee
4. Abolition of the Minimum Support Price system
Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: These reforms remove market fragmentation and repeated fees so that traders can buy across mandis within a state. eNAM has nothing to do with MSP, which continues as a separate price support policy.

questions.q: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission, launched in 2014, is primarily aimed at:
o: Promotion of fodder cultivation on wasteland
Conservation and development of indigenous bovine breeds
questions.e: The mission supports genetic upgradation and conservation of native cattle breeds through breeding centres and better bull and semen production. Setting up the milk grid is associated with Operation Flood.
questions.s: PIB (Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about pulses in India:
1. India is the largest producer of pulses in the world.
2. India is also the largest consumer of pulses in the world.
3. India is the largest exporter of pulses in the world.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India produces and consumes more pulses than any other country, yet domestic demand often exceeds supply, so it also imports large quantities. This is why it is described as the largest importer, not exporter.
